h: Getting the most from a day at Hayton
p: Hayton is a small village a few miles north-east of Retford, surrounded by flat farmland and quiet lanes, which is just the setting you want for a peaceful day on the bank. Arrive with the car packed sensibly so you're not lugging gear back and forth, and if you're new to the place, have a gentle walk round before choosing a peg. Watching where fish are topping or where other anglers are getting bites can save you hours.

A few essentials make all the difference. Anyone aged 13 or over needs an Environment Agency rod licence to fish in England, and it's free for under-17s, though they still need to have one. Pack an unhooking mat, a landing net and a disgorger, and expect the specimen waters in particular to have stricter rules on rigs, bait and fish care. Big carp are precious, so handle them carefully, keep them wet and get them back quickly.

For families bringing youngsters along, keep the first session short and simple: a float rod, a pint of maggots and a margin swim where they can see the float easily. A couple of quick bites will hook them for life far better than hours of waiting for one big fish.

Between sessions, the Chesterfield Canal winds through this part of north Nottinghamshire, offering easy towpath walking, and Retford town centre has cafés, pubs and shops for picking up anything you've forgotten.
